To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the WAF domain is projected by 95% of the models at 1. 5 ◦C global warming and by 100% of the models by 2 ◦ C global warming to have more frequent and intense heat waves, and that the Sahel region is projected by 90% of the models, by 1.5◦ C global warming, to experience the strongest increase of dry spells and the strongest decrease of the standardized precipitation evaporation index.
the most intense warming is projected over the drier parts of the Sahel and that the ‘dry will get drier, wet will get wetter’ paradigm will be broken.

the Sahel is projected to experience the strongest increase in temperature and the most significant drying in the WAF region, while the Guinea Coast and central Africa will experience a significant increase of heavy rainfall and an increase in temperature.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the implications for the WAF domain of the Paris Agreement, which aims to limit global warming to 1.5◦C or 2◦C above pre-industrial levels.
the implications of the Paris Agreement on climate extremes in West and Central Africa.
the following questions: (i) How do changes in climate extremes vary across sub-regions in the WAF?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the WAF region will experience an increase of the frequency, duration and intensity of extreme events with global warming, with a higher increase in the drier regions than in the wetter ones.
the climate of the WAF domain is projected to become warmer, drier and more variable.
the climate of the Sahel region will get drier, while the climate of the wetter parts of WAF will become wetter.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
at 1. 5 ◦C, the Sahel is expected to be the driest, the eastern part of the Sahel will be drier than the western part, and the western Sahel is expected the warmest.

at 1.6◦C global warming, the Sahelian region will experience a significant increase in temperature, heat waves and dry spells, while the wet regions will experience an increase in extreme precipitation events and heavy rainfall.

the WAF domain will be characterized by more frequent and more intense extreme heat events and more frequent and more severe drought events, while the frequency of heavy rainfall events will increase.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the subregional scale is a key factor in understanding the impact of global warming on the WAF domain, as it allows to capture the regional heterogeneities of climate change and its impacts.
climate extremes will change at subregional level and that the impacts will vary across the WAF domain.
, at a global warming above 2◦C, the climate extremes in West and Central Africa will become more intense and more frequent, and will be more likely to occur in the drier regions.
